Checks of one value, compared

Source: R/checks.R
checks.Rd

checks() lists every check a project's documents make on a value and groups them by value, so that a value checked in several places with conditions that differ a little (x > 5 here, x >= 5 there) shows. A check is a guard (each comma part of a one-arm if), a check argument of a claim(), or, here only, a comma part of a two-arm if, which chooses wording and fails nothing (a branch). Only checks weft can read are compared: a comparison whose sides are names, dictionary reads, expressions such as max(turbidity) and literals, or a bool name; the rest are listed under not read. Nothing in a document is run.

Usage

checks(path = ".", files = NULL, repeats = 3L)

# S3 method for class 'weft_checks'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

path

One existing file or folder. The project root is found from it.

files

NULL, or documents (relative to the root or absolute under it) to report on.

repeats

A whole number from 2: how many places make a hint.

x

A weft_checks.

...

Not used.

Value

A weft_checks data frame, one row per check, with columns file, line, role, level, value, op, other, cond (NA when the check is not readable), text, always, rebound, flag and repeated, and the attribute notes. Printing it shows the report.

Details

A value is flagged when two of its checks compare it with the same other operand under operators that differ only in strictness (operators), or with different literals in one direction (literals). The report hints at checks made in repeats places or more with the same condition: check once, where the value is made.

Examples

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "checks-example")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(c("The site [exceeded]{if=\"flow > limit\"} the limit.", "",
             "In March it [reached]{if=\"flow >= limit\"} the limit."), file.path(dir, "report.Rmd"))
checks(dir)
#> weft checks: 2 checks of 1 value in 1 document; 1 value flagged
#> 
#> report.Rmd
#>   flow  [operators]
#>     flow > limit   1  line 1
#>     flow >= limit  1  line 3
#>
